title: Elmira Road North apartment rezoning approved
subtitle: Eramosa Road heritage designation deferred, new heritage notices, transition zoning extension and growth monitoring report.
overview: Council approved an Official Plan and zoning change at 105 Elmira Road North. It allows a medium density residential rental apartment development on a site that was zoned for neighbourhood commercial use {{vote:m16}}. Nearby residents raised concerns about density and overflow parking, and some councillors voted against the change.

Council deferred a decision on designating 30 and 32 Eramosa Road under the Ontario Heritage Act after the owners objected {{vote:m18}}. The deferral set no timeline, and the mayor encouraged the owners and staff to keep talking. Council also began the designation process for a number of properties, including several on Norwich Street West and Surrey Street East, and approved the designation of 56 Paisley Street despite a notice of objection.

Council extended transition provisions in the 2023 zoning by-law for specific properties with active site plan applications. It also approved the Connecting Links funding agreement for York Road reconstruction and received the 2024 growth monitoring report. That report showed fewer new housing units than in recent years and a tough market for builders.

decisions.detail: Council approved an Official Plan amendment and site-specific Medium Density Residential zoning to permit the proposed apartment development at the corner of Elmira Road North and Willow Road {{vote:m16}}.
Council deferred the objection and designation by-law for 30 and 32 Eramosa Road, with no return date set {{vote:m18}}.
Council approved a City-initiated amendment giving specific properties with active site plan applications extra time to proceed under the former 1995 zoning rules.
Council received the owners' notice of objection and approved the designation by-law for 56 Paisley Street.
The Clerk may publish notice of intention to designate 1 Norwich Street West; similar separate motions covered other Norwich Street West, Woolwich, Gordon, Surrey and Paisley street properties.

Council directed the City Treasurer to sign a contribution agreement with the Ministry of Transportation for Connecting Links funding and recognized the first contract for the York Road Phase 4 reconstruction.
Council received the 2024 Growth Management and Affordable Housing Monitoring Report.

debate: On 105 Elmira Road North, the applicant's team said the plan added three-bedroom units, more visitor parking, fencing and trees. They said the existing zoning already allows a six-storey mixed-use building and that site-specific provisions are common and backed by technical studies.

A resident delegate called the Elmira Road proposal an overdevelopment. Concerns were density well above zoning limits, all-surface parking, overflow parking on nearby streets, and traffic safety for children. One councillor who voted against said the density was too high and the parking too low, and suggested stacked townhomes instead.

On Eramosa Road, staff described the building as one of the city's oldest surviving industrial structures. The owner delegate said the owners received only a few days' notice before the heritage committee considered the property, disputed the building's heritage attributes, and cited insurance concerns and a lack of incentives.

Staff said insurance policies vary by company and that the city lists heritage-friendly insurers. Staff also said financial incentives would come with the Ward West heritage district plan. A councillor who moved the deferral noted council had deferred a similar case a month earlier, and the mayor said the deferral set no timeline.

On the growth report, councillors and the mayor said housing starts are held back by high costs, financing, trade uncertainty and federal GST uncertainty, not by city approvals. Staff said many approved units are ready but not being built, and one councillor asked whether a use-it-or-lose-it approach was needed. Staff said provincial rules already limit approval periods.
